full_judgment: 4. The case of the writ-petitioner as made out in the writ petition and in the  supplementary affidavits was that he took loan of Taka 11,87,000 (Eleven Lakh Eighty Seven Thousand) only from writ-respondent No. 2, Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, respondent No. 3 herein (hereinafter referred to as the Corporation), in 1979 for construction of a multistoried building on his land measuring 18 decimals situated within Narayangonj town and with that loan money, the writ-petitioner constructed a four storied building on that land and had been living there with his family. As security of that loan, the writ-petitioner mortgaged the said building along with the land to the Corporation. The writ-petitioner failed to repay the loan as per stipulation and consequently, the Corporation filed Miscellaneous Case No.16 of 1989 before the District Judge, Narayangonj under article 27 of Bangladesh Housing Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (PO No. 7 of 1973) against the writ-petitioner. Subsequently, Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1989 was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj for disposal and it was registered as Artha Rin Mortgage Suit No.152 of 1991. Eventually, the mortgaged suit was decreed. The Corporation as decree-holder levied Mortgage Execution Case No. 59 of 1994 before the Artha Rin Adalat for execution of the decree by selling the mortgaged property in auction. In the execution case, the writ-petitioner appeared and entered into agreement with the decree-holder-corporation and the execution case was disposed of in terms of the solenama filed by both the parties. But as the writ-petitioner failed to repay the outstanding loan as per terms and conditions of the solenama the said execution case was revived on the prayer of the decree-holder-corporation and eventually, the mortgaged property was put in auction on 10-11-2008. In the auction, three bidders participated of whom the added writ-respondent No. 3, Md Selim Hossain, petitioner (hereinafter referred to as auction purchaser-petitioner) became the highest bidder at Taka 28,00,000 (Twenty Eight Lakh) only. The decree-holder-corporation filed an application before the executing Court praying for cancelling the auction sale on the ground of low price. The application was rejected. Thereafter, on 24-11-2008, the writ-petitioner filed an application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 praying for cancellation of the auction sale stating, inter alia, that the decree-holder-corporation, had already allowed reschedulement for payment of the outstanding loan and he had been paying the loan money according to that reschedulement; after re-schedulement, the writ-petitioner paid a big chunk of money to the decree-holder-corporation, but it without intimating anything to the writ-petitioner revived the execution case and behind his back sold the property in auction at Taka 28,00,000 (Twenty Eight Lakh) only on 10-11-2008 though the property is valued at Taka 1 (one) crore; the actual price of the property in question was initially assessed by the decree-holder-corporation at Taka 87,00,000 (Eighty Seven Lath) and the same was accepted by the Artha Rin Adalat by order dated 10-8-2005. The application was rejected by the Artha Rin Adalat by the order dated 11-1-2008. The decree-holder-corporation filed an application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure for cancellation of the auction sale. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2008. The Artha Rin Adalat dismissed the miscellaneous case. Against that, the decree-holder-corporation filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 6 of 2009 before the District Judge, Narayangonj which was pending. In the above background, the writ-petitioner filed the writ petition.
